Fixed in `rich/pretty.py:783` — the dataclass branch of `traverse` now skips `repr=True` fields the instance doesn't actually have (`hasattr(obj, field.name)`), so an unassigned `field(init=False)` no longer raises `AttributeError` and `BadDataclass()` prints via the node's `empty` repr.

`python -m pytest -q tests/test_pretty.py`: 50 passed, 1 skipped.

argv:
Bug report for this repository (rich):

Printing a dataclass instance with `Console().print(obj)` (or `pretty_repr`) raises
`AttributeError` when one of its fields was declared with `field(init=False)` and never
assigned, e.g.

    @dataclass(eq=False)
    class BadDataclass:
        item: int = field(init=False)

    console.print(BadDataclass())

The pretty printer walks every field with `repr=True` and reads it off the instance. A field
the instance does not actually have should simply be skipped, so the example prints
`BadDataclass()`.

Change as little as possible and do not edit the tests. The test command is
`python -m pytest -q tests/test_pretty.py`; run it once at the end.
